description:
We're Astravelle — four ambitious minds driven by curiosity, creativity, and technology. With skills in web development, mobile apps, and project management, we're ready to turn NASA's data into impactful solutions.

We're looking for teammates interested in Python, AI/ML, data analysis, Earth science, visualization, and UI/UX design. We value fresh ideas, teamwork, and a willingness to learn.

Bring your curiosity. Let's build something extraordinary! 🚀
summary: TrendLens helps agricultural planners and water-management researchers explore whether unusually hot and dry days are becoming more frequent around Minya, Egypt. Using NASA GLDAS-2.1 Noah data accessed through Giovanni, we developed an interactive dashboard covering 2001–2023 for one rectangular study area. It identifies compound hot-and-dry days, displays annual frequency and conditional proportions, and compares nine event definitions alongside trend estimates and uncertainty. The primary definition identifies 126 compound days among 8,400 valid days. Results remain exploratory and do not establish a reliable increase. TrendLens makes uncertainty and sensitivity visible, allowing users to understand how conclusions depend on analytical choices. Users can inspect the study footprint, compare definitions, and download evidence reports to support research and planning.
details:
TrendLens addresses the Earth System Trend Detective challenge by investigating historical changes in concurrent high temperature and low root-zone soil moisture. It is designed for agricultural planners, water-management researchers, and students who need to understand environmental patterns together with the strength and limitations of the evidence.

Our analysis uses NASA GLDAS-2.1 Noah data accessed through Giovanni for a rectangular study area around Minya, Upper Egypt: 30–31° east and 27–28.95° north. Each daily record represents the region as a whole. Temperature is the highest available value among eight three-hourly regional readings per day. Soil moisture is the daily mean of the native GLDAS RootMoist variable, expressed in kg/m² and understood as a model estimate.

We use 2001–2023 as both the study period and the fixed reference period. Thresholds are calculated separately for each calendar month. A compound day occurs when temperature is at or above its heat threshold and RootMoist is at or below its moisture threshold on the same valid day.

The dashboard distinguishes two indicators: the percentage of all valid days that were both hot and dry, and the historical percentage of valid hot days that were also dry. It displays annual counts, coverage, Theil–Sen trend slopes, trend-test results, adjusted statistical values, and uncertainty intervals.

Our sensitivity explorer compares nine definitions, combining heat percentiles of 90, 92.5, and 95 with moisture percentiles of 10, 15, and 20. Full-year and June–August results are available separately. The primary full-year definition identifies 126 compound days among 8,400 valid days, with 845 hot days.

The findings remain exploratory. Some methods and definitions disagree, and the evidence does not establish a reliable environmental increase. Insufficient evidence does not prove that no change occurred. Approximate uncertainty intervals also depend on assumptions that have not been independently verified.

We developed the analysis in Python using NumPy, pandas, SciPy, pymannkendall, and openpyxl. The current frontend uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Leaflet. It includes satellite/street maps, synchronized filters, separate analysis pages, light/dark modes, and downloadable evidence.

Our contribution is making the reliability of environmental evidence understandable: users can see how changing a reasonable definition affects the results. Satellite imagery provides geographic context only. The project does not claim farm-level measurements, district rankings, forecasts, causal explanations, or irrigation recommendations.
